title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

title: Brazil’s stock exchange pushes stablecoin launch back to 2027
summary: Brazil’s stock exchange is working with six major financial institutions on a real-backed stablecoin that could launch as early as the first quarter of 2027.

title: Austria-supervised crypto firms report 20.4B euros in H1 trading volume
summary: About 74% of accounts were based in other EEA countries, highlighting the market’s cross-border nature and putting Europe’s supervisory framework in focus, FMA said.

title: Bitcoin supply metric hits 11-year low as new ‘capitulation’ signal arrives
summary: The seven-day moving average of Bitcoin’s supply profit/loss ratio hit an 11-year low as BTC price losses month-to-date remain near 20%.

title: Bluefin to shut down perps, refocus on spot trading and tokenized RWAs
summary: Bluefin will close its perps platform on Dec. 4, exiting a shrinking Sui market where it once handled over $500 million in daily trades.

title: ESMA to overhaul EU’s MiCA crypto register in 2027
summary: ESMA’s new MiCA register will replace manual reporting and introduce automated data checks and a version history for crypto white papers.

title: New York AG secures $1.37B court judgment against NovaTech founders
summary: The judgment follows an August 2025 default ruling against the founders over a Ponzi scheme that targeted Haitian and other immigrant communities.

title: Japan’s crypto security group taps SEAL to speed up hack response
summary: The partnership comes weeks after a third-party data breach exposed hundreds of thousands of customer email addresses belonging to two Japanese crypto exchanges.

title: Ethereum devs set Glamsterdam’s Hoodi rollout for mid-December after delays
summary: Glamsterdam’s Hoodi upgrade was delayed in October after concerns that changes to gas pricing could break some existing smart contracts.

title: AI is driving a flood of crypto bug reports. Now it’s helping sort them
summary: Bug bounty platform HackerOne said it’s increasing its triage throughput with AI agents after a record quarter of reports in the third quarter.
